name: California
source: gun-policy Season 3 Stage 5, California hand-over (ca/HANDOVER-A.md part 7, ca/MEASURES-B.md, write/ca-01/recipe.json), 2026-11-13
sessions: Two-year sessions that start in odd years. No special sessions in LegiScan.

votes.floor_rule: LegiScan's roll calls include committee votes: a floor vote is a passage motion whose total is 30 or more (Assembly 80 seats, Senate 40). Consent-calendar votes count as passage.
gaps: Official vote pages print surnames only.

texts.marks: leginfo HTML: added words are blue italic (saved as {+ +}), struck words red (saved as [- -]).
texts.note: Bills are often introduced as spot bills whose real text arrives later: read a sponsor-only bill at its last version.

reader_access.leginfo.legislature.ca.gov: blocked: a plain fetch gets a Cloudflare 403 (an earlier topic used Wayback copies)

search_note: California sponsorships and Assembly and Senate floor votes on this topic come from the bulk bill data (listed above): skip the legislature's sponsor lists and vote pages (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov answers a plain fetch with a 403), and add the place "sponsor list: covered by bulk bill data". Spend the search on their own words (statements, campaign pages, newsletters, floor remarks, interviews, questionnaires). If any page returns 403, an empty page or a bot check, record it as blocked and move on: do not retry it with a different user agent, headers or tool.
bill_table_note:
- California bill text marks changes to existing law; `operative_text` quotes the law as the bill leaves it. Where the instrument's `provenance.note` says an earlier version differs, the earlier chamber vote was on that wording: say so in `why` and flag it if the rung would differ.
- Each instrument's `votes[].note` names the text version each roll call was taken on.
quirks: Name matching: LegiScan lists some members with a title ("Dr.") or a two-part surname. 10 older idmap.tsv lines pointed senators at the wrong chamber's record (fixed 2026-11-13): check every line against name and chamber.
Long records: a median of 57 record findings a person, up to 144. Record-only coding cost twice Missouri's per person.
